subject: Quantix: sustained p99 increase for long-history requests (16k/32k) — action plan
messages:
From: Devon Hayes <devon.hayes@quantix.ai>
To: support@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: Paula Mendes <paula.mendes@quantix.ai>
Date: Mon, 3 Sep 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Major p99 spike for long-history requests (16k/32k)

Hi Redwood team,

We're seeing a sustained increase in p99 latency for requests that include long conversation histories (16k+/32k token windows) starting ~08:40 PDT this morning. Impact: our user-facing summarization jobs are timing out ~3-4x more frequently and throughput has dropped by ~35% on hosted API. Error rates (502/504) increased during the spike.

Quick details we captured:
- Region: us-west-2
- Example request IDs: req_7f4a2b, req_7f4a8d, req_7f4b1c
- Typical p99 before: ~1.1s; current p99: 4.8s for 16k, 9.2s for 32k
- No config change on our end; we did not increase concurrency.

This is customer-critical — can someone please confirm you're on it and share the immediate mitigation steps? We're preparing an incident call if helpful.

Thanks,
Devon
Devon Hayes
Head of Platform — Quantix
[attachment: quantix-traces-20280903.tar.gz]
From: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: aditya.rao@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 3 Sep 2028 09:24:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Major p99 spike for long-history requests (16k/32k)

Forwarding Quantix escalation — they report p99 jumps on long-history requests and higher 5xx. I’ve queued SRE and runtime folks. Immediate asks:

1) Capture end-to-end traces and KV cache hit rates for the affected request IDs (Devon attached traces).
2) Check if a recent kernel selection or quantization profile pushed to hosted API at ~08:30 PDT correlates.
3) Evaluate short-term mitigations: model-variant fallback (smaller context-optimized variant), prefix cache warm, or tenant-level rate limiting.

Can @aditya and @marissa lead this? I’ll loop in LAURA for visibility and exec summary after we have an initial RCA.

Karthik
VP, Product — Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference
From: aditya_rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: quantix-sre@quantix.ai
Date: Mon, 3 Sep 2028 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Major p99 spike for long-history requests (16k/32k)

On it — initial findings below after 30m triage.

Summary:
- We observed a significant increase in KV cache miss rate for sequences >12k tokens in the us-west-2 pool starting 08:38 PDT. Miss rate jumped from ~6% -> ~48% on the affected hosts.
- A lightweight kernel rollout (quant-opt-v2) was promoted to a subset of hosts at 08:33 PDT for performance testing; that rollout shows higher memory pressure for long KV chains which appears to force extra LRU evictions and replay work.
- Correlated alerts: ALRT-7782 shows increased disk IO on the cache nodes backing that hostgroup.

Immediate mitigations taken:
- Rolled back quant-opt-v2 from the affected hostgroup at 09:01 PDT (workload draining in progress).
- Increased prefix cache retention threshold for Quantix tenant in us-west-2 to reduce misses (temporary).
- Opened a canary route to route 10% of Quantix long-history traffic to a stable model-variant (ctx-optimized-v1) at 09:12 PDT.

Attachments: latency-snapshot-20280903.csv (summary of per-host p95/p99), quantix-traces-20280903.tar.gz (selected traces sent by customer).

Next steps:
- Deeper heap/memory profile of quant-opt-v2 kernel to validate eviction behavior (owner: runtime team).
- Restore normal prefix retention once hosts warm up (~30–60m).
- Schedule 11:00 PDT stand-up with Quantix SRE to confirm if mitigations reduce observed errors.

Aditya Rao
Sr. Engineering Manager, Runtime
[attachment: latency-snapshot-20280903.csv]
From: Quantix SRE <sre@quantix.ai>
To: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, aditya.rao@redwood.ai
Cc: Devon Hayes <devon.hayes@quantix.ai>, paula.mendes@quantix.ai
Date: Mon, 3 Sep 2028 10:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Major p99 spike for long-history requests (16k/32k)

Thanks — we appreciate the quick response. We'll join the 11:00 PDT call. A couple of requests:
- Can you provide a short exec-friendly summary of customer impact (estimated user-facing timeouts, revenue impact if any) for our leadership?
- Please confirm the traffic percentage being routed to ctx-optimized-v1 and whether fallbacks are automatic if errors continue.

Also, we're going to lower our internal long-history concurrency to 50% for the next hour to reduce pressure; we'll monitor.

— Quantix SRE
From: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Devon Hayes <devon.hayes@quantix.ai>, sre@quantix.ai
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, aditya.rao@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 3 Sep 2028 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Major p99 spike for long-history requests (16k/32k)

Devon / Quantix team — thank you for the quick cooperation. Exec summary below we will use for broader communication: 

Executive brief (11:05 PDT):
- Impact: Quantix saw p99 increases on long-history requests (16k/32k) starting 08:38 PDT with increased 5xxs and ~35% throughput drop for summarization flows. Estimated user-facing timeouts increased by ~2.8% of hourly jobs during the window; no confirmed revenue-impacting outages at this time.
- Root cause (initial): Interaction between the recently promoted quant-opt-v2 kernel and long KV cache chains causing elevated memory pressure and higher eviction/replay rates on a subset of us-west-2 hosts.
- Mitigation: quant-opt-v2 rollback completed to affected hostgroup; prefix cache retention increased for tenant; 10% of long-history traffic routed to ctx-optimized-v1 as a canary.
- Next steps: full runtime profiling of quant-opt-v2 (owner: runtime), monitor for 2 hours, consider a coordinated slower rollout with cache warmup and telemetry gating.
- SLA/credits: We will compile a formal incident report and any credit recommendations after full RCA.

We will join your 11:00 PDT call to review live metrics. Appended attachments include the per-host latency snapshot and selected traces.

Karthik
From: Paula Mendes <paula.mendes@quantix.ai>
To: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, aditya.rao@redwood.ai
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 3 Sep 2028 14:37:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Major p99 spike for long-history requests (16k/32k)

All — after the rollback and canary routing we saw p99 drop back toward baseline for the canary traffic and error rates stabilized. Our downstream ingestion backlog recovered to normal levels by ~13:50 PDT. Thank you for the quick investigation and transparent updates.

Please proceed with the runtime profiling and send the RCA when available. Also, we'll want a short postmortem we can share with our ops team and a three-point mitigation plan (short-term, medium, long).

Paula Mendes
Head of Operations — Quantix
